subject: Throughput SLA: metric definitions and acceptance harness for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Alex Duarte <alex@cloudline.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudline.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — metric clarification

Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement and infra teams are aligning on the Dedicated commitment and we'd like to lock down exactly how Redwood defines the throughput guarantee so we can sign off on contracts.

Specifically:
- Do you guarantee tokens/sec, requests/sec, or both? How are tokens counted (input+output, tokenizer used)?
- What's the latency SLO per request (p50/p95/p99) and how does that factor into credits/penalties?
- We'll need a measurement harness and a runbook for acceptance testing during onboarding.

Can you share a concise definition and a proposed measurement plan we can review with legal and SRE? Also attaching the draft procurement checklist for context.

Appreciate it,

Alex
VP of Engineering
Cloudline.ai

Attachment: procurement_checklist_v1.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Duarte <alex@cloudline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — metric clarification

Alex — thanks, great questions. High level replies below and a proposed next step (short acceptance harness + runbook).

High-level definitions
- Tokens/sec: we count generated + consumed tokens using the model's tokenizer (BPE/byte-level depending on model). We'll include the tokenizer version in the evidence bundle.
- Requests/sec: number of inference requests completed per second (request completes when final token(s) returned or a configured early-exit is triggered).
- Guarantees: we can provide a primary guarantee on sustained tokens/sec at a fixed token length distribution (profiled from your sample traffic), and an availability-style guarantee on requests/sec for tails (p95) to capture latency spikes.

Latency targets
- p50/p95/p99 measured on end-to-end request completion in our serving topology. Recommended targets for your commit tier (8x A100-equivalent pool): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 420ms, p99 < 1.2s for conversational workloads at 512-token horizon. We can tune depending on your 99th-percentile appetite.

Measurement methodology (proposal)
- Baseline profile: you provide a 48-hour representative trace (anonymized). We derive the token length histogram and request concurrency profile.
- Benchmark harness: Redwood will run a 4-hour continuous run against a dedicated staging pool that mirrors the committed pool (attached baseline_benchmark_script.py). Tests include steady-state sustained token injection and short spike runs for tail behavior.
- Evidence bundle: raw traces (sample_trace_20260821.json), tokenizer versions, kernel config, and a short summary CSV with tokens/sec and latency percentiles.
- Acceptance: pass if sustained tokens/sec >= 95% of committed with p95 latency within agreed band for 4 hours.

Next steps
1) I'll loop in Karthik to outline the exact harness and acceptance thresholds.
2) We'll attach a draft SLA redline (SLA_draft_Cloudline_v2.docx) with credit model options.

If this aligns, can procurement confirm the committed token band (you mentioned 120M tokens/day target) and whether you'd prefer a tokens-first or RPS-first guarantee? Considerations below.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: baseline_benchmark_script.py

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated throughput guarantees — metric clarification

Quick notes for pricing negotiation:
- If Cloudline wants a tokens/sec guarantee tied to tight p95/p99, we should ask for a higher commit band or stronger price protection. Tighter SLOs imply higher reserve costs.
- Consider offering a blended guarantee: tokens/sec baseline (sustained) + a soft RPS tail guarantee with credits rather than hard SLA (limits downside exposure).
- Discount ask: We can offer 15% off sticker for a 12-month commit at 130M tokens/day with a 95% sustained tokens/sec guarantee, stepping to 20% with a 24-month.

Marissa / Karthik — any pushback operationally on the acceptance gating (4-hour run) vs a longer soak test?

-Ben

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — metric clarification

Adding technical specifics for the runbook and acceptance criteria (for the evidence bundle):

Runbook highlights
- Token counting: we'll ship a tokenizer shim that normalizes token counts across model variants; all benchmark runs must use that shim to avoid discrepancies.
- Test harness pieces: load generator (our script), collector (zipkin-compatible traces), and summary exporter (tokens/sec, qps, p50/p95/p99). See baseline_benchmark_script.py for orchestration.
- Measurement windows: 4h steady-state window for sustained measurement, with 15m spike injections every 60m to exercise queues.

Acceptance gates
- Sustained tokens/sec >= 0.95 * committed_tokens/sec over the 4h window.
- p95 latency <= agreed threshold for your tier (default 420ms); if p95 breaches but sustained tokens/sec is met, we apply a de-escalation credit schedule (first breach: monitoring alert, second within 30d: 5% credit, third: 10%).
- Clock sync and immutable evidence: timestamps must be NTP-synced; we'll provide SHA256 hashes for artifact integrity.

Operational notes
- We'll provision a staging pool identical in size to the committed pool for acceptance runs. Staging runs will be scheduled mutually and may require a 3-business-day lead.
- If Cloudline requests additional instrumentation (custom tracing or business-metric correlation), that can be scoped as an add-on professional service.

I'll draft the technical appendix and attach the initial harness results after the first run.

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample_trace_20260821.json

From: Sara Hsu <sara@cloudline.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Duarte <alex@cloudline.ai>, procurement@cloudline.ai
Date: 2026-08-26T14:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — metric clarification

Tessa/Karthik/Ben — this is helpful, thanks. Cloudline is aligned with a tokens-first guarantee but we'd like the option to shift to an RPS-first guarantee if our prompt lengths change materially (we'll provide updated traces).

Two asks before procurement signs:
1) Could you add the exact credit table (percent credit vs number of breaches) into the SLA draft? We prefer a deterministic schedule.
2) Please confirm the lead time to schedule the staging acceptance run and whether we can run a second, longer soak (24h) for an incremental fee.

If we can get those items in SLA_draft_Cloudline_v2.docx and a short runbook summary, procurement will circulate for final redlines.

Best,

Sara Hsu
Head of Procurement
Cloudline.ai

Attachment: procurement_constraints.xlsx
